I am 70 this year, and I have worked this land since I was 15 years old. My father taught me, and now I manage 30 mu — that is a good-sized piece around Quzhou. I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer, wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone here. Last year my wheat gave me about 1000 jin per mu, and the maize gave about 1200 jin per mu. I need to keep that up because my grandson is in high school and the fees are not small.

For the wheat, I plant the improved seed that Old Zhang at the supply store gives me — the one in the blue bag that most people buy. When I plant in October, I put one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, 50 kg. It is the 18-20-6 kind. Then in early March, when the wheat turns green after winter, I spread another 30 kg of urea per mu. The dealer tried to sell me some slow-release fancy stuff last year, but it is 30 yuan more per bag. I have used regular urea for 40 years and it works. I rotary-till the field after the maize comes off, then plant the wheat. I irrigate three times: once right after planting to help it sprout, once in late March before I put the urea down, and once when the heads come out in May. My well is good this year. I spray twice — herbicide in the spring, and fungicide once if the weather turns wet. I expect around 1000 jin per mu, which is 500 kg, maybe 520 if the weather helps.

For the summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off the combine in early June, I get the planter in the field. No time to plough — I sow directly into the wheat stubble, no-tillage. I use hybrid seed, about 2 kg per mu. I put 50 kg of compound fertilizer in the drill when I sow — the 28-6-6 kind, that is 100 jin. I do not topdress the maize much; some years I put a little urea at the big trumpet stage, but last year I did not and it still did fine. The well lets me irrigate twice: once when the plants are knee-high, and once when the tassels show. If the rains come, maybe I skip one, but I watch the sky. I spray twice too — herbicide at sowing, and then I watch for the corn borer. If I see them, I spray. I usually see them. I expect about 1200 jin per mu, which is 600 kg.

I think about money every day. Six people in the house, and the grandchildren need school fees. One bag of compound is about 160 yuan, urea is about 120 yuan. For 30 mu, that is thousands of yuan just for fertilizer. But if I cut back and the yield drops, I lose much more than I save. My son sends some money from his factory job, but the land is what feeds us. I would rather put on a little too much than too little. A bad year is a disaster I cannot afford.
